facts.text: A collision is a machine striking a person, a vehicle, another machine or a fixed object.
facts.quote: A collision is a machine striking a person, a vehicle, another machine or a fixed object

facts.text: On job sites, a small number of collision types cause most collision deaths.
facts.quote: on job sites a small number of collision types cause most of the deaths.

facts.text: The booklet distinguishes collisions from near misses with no contact and from non-collision accidents such as a truck going through a berm or rolling over; an object-detecting system can address only the collision group.
facts.quote: a near miss (no contact) and a non-collision accident such as a truck going through a berm or rolling over. The separation matters because an object-detecting system can only address the first group.

facts.text: The booklet ranks collision situations by harm using fatality data from several countries.
facts.quote: The booklet ranks collision situations by harm, using fatality data from several countries [Chapter 4]

facts.text: A large haul truck crushing a light vehicle in front of it, often when starting from rest, accounted for 5 of 13 US haul-truck collision deaths from 2005 to 2021.
facts.quote: A large haul truck crushes a light vehicle in front of it, often when starting from rest (5 of 13 US haul-truck collision deaths, 2005 to 2021).

facts.text: A smaller dump truck or loader reversing over a worker on foot or a small vehicle accounted for 67% of 22 US blind-area deaths from 2000 to 2006.
facts.quote: A smaller dump truck or loader reverses over a worker on foot or a small vehicle (67% of 22 US blind-area deaths, 2000 to 2006).

facts.text: The collision-harm ranking includes people on foot struck or pinned during other movements, especially underground, citing 39 continuous-miner deaths from 1984 to 2015.
facts.quote: A person on foot is struck or pinned in other movements, above all underground (39 continuous-miner deaths, 1984 to 2015).

facts.text: Loss of control through a berm, reverse-overs or ground failure at a dump point constituted the largest group of haul-truck deaths, 33 of 54, but were not object collisions.
facts.quote: Loss of control through a berm, and reverse-overs or ground failure at a dump point: the largest group of haul-truck deaths (33 of 54), but not object collisions.

facts.text: The collision-harm ranking cites 131 backing deaths involving workers on foot at road construction sites from 1992 to 2010.
facts.quote: A worker on foot struck at a road construction site (131 backing deaths, 1992 to 2010).

facts.text: Heavy-machine collisions with other heavy machines at tip heads, loading areas and haul roads mostly cause property damage.
facts.quote: Heavy machine against heavy machine at tip heads, loading areas and haul roads: mostly property damage

facts.text: Heavy-machine collisions with other heavy machines at tip heads, loading areas and haul roads are the most frequently reported collision type in regulator data.
facts.quote: Heavy machine against heavy machine at tip heads, loading areas and haul roads: mostly property damage, and the most frequently reported collision type in regulator data.

facts.text: Underground LHD collisions, collisions during an intentional loading approach, contact with fixed structures and swing strikes rank lower in the booklet's collision-harm ranking; frequency data for these situations were not found.
facts.quote: Lower come underground LHD collisions, collisions during an intentional loading approach, contact with fixed structures, and swing strikes, for which frequency data were not found [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Collision databases record deaths far better than damage-only collisions.
facts.quote: Databases record deaths far better than damage-only collisions

facts.text: Collision figures from different countries must not be added into one international rate because agencies use different categories.
facts.quote: agencies use different categories, so numbers from different countries must not be added into one international rate [Chapter 4].

facts.text: In 2025, powered haulage caused 13 of 33 US mining deaths (39%); powered haulage is a category broader than object collisions.
facts.quote: in 2025 powered haulage caused 13 of 33 US mining deaths (39%), a category wider than object collisions [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The collision-mitigation program should prioritize scenarios involving a truck starting forward with a light vehicle in front, a loader or truck reversing over a person, and close machine-to-machine work.
facts.quote: The ranking tells the program which scenarios to prioritize: a truck starting forward with a light vehicle in front, a loader or truck reversing over a person, and close machine-to-machine work.

facts.text: A system detecting only vehicles and people addresses an important but incomplete part of the fatal-risk picture.
facts.quote: a system detecting only vehicles and people "addresses an important but incomplete part of the fatal-risk picture" [Chapter 4].
